key_insight: A large-scale sweep of quantum neural network design choices shows that circuit structure matters more than parameter count, and the best QNN can beat a classical BiLSTM on GBP/USD forecasting.
engineering_relevance: The results give practical design rules for choosing encodings, ansatzes, qubit counts, depth, and loss functions when building QNNs for regression and time-series tasks.
method: Grid-searched 1,368 QNN configurations across encoding, ansatz, qubits, depth, and cost function.
Evaluated each model on financial time-series forecasting using the GBP/USD spot exchange rate.
Compared simulated performance, convergence, and computational cost, then tested noise sensitivity on IQM Emerald hardware.
evidence_signal: The best QNN reached an R² of 0.985 and outperformed a classical BiLSTM baseline, while hardware runs exposed strong sensitivity to gate errors and decoherence.
watch_item: Performance gains may not transfer directly to real devices because circuit depth and gate choice strongly affect noise resilience on near-term hardware.
paper_title: Large-Scale Benchmarking of Quantum Neural Network Configurations for Financial Time Series Forecasting
